assumptions_made: The Hugging Face dataset argilla/synthetic-text-classification-news was used as the primary source for news text and sentiment labels, falling back to synthetic generation if loading failed
The BERT-based sentiment analysis model was initialized with cardiffnlp/twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest
The weak supervision framework was simulated through direct aggregation of sentiment labels into a policy uncertainty index
Synthetic unemployment and macroeconomic data were generated with realistic temporal dependencies and correlations
The sklearn metrics functions were modified to avoid the 'squared' parameter issue by manually computing RMSE
The experiment was designed to run on a single GPU node with sufficient memory for the BERT model

results.hypothesis: To determine whether policy uncertainty derived from news text using a BERT-based sentiment analysis model and aggregated via a weak supervision framework exhibits a stronger predictive correlation with subsequent regional unemployment changes compared to lagged unemployment alone, while controlling for macroeconomic trends.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Model using only lagged unemployment as predictor
results.success_criteria: If the model incorporating policy uncertainty from news text achieves significantly higher R-squared values and lower MAE/RMSE compared to the baseline model, the hypothesis is supported. If not, the hypothesis is refuted.
results.notes:
Policy uncertainty from news text did not show significant improvement.
MAE did not improve by at least 0.5%.
RMSE did not improve by at least 0.5%.
results.methodological_validity: mixed real and synthetic inputs — findings are NOT interpretable as evidence; the synthetic inputs are listed in data_provenance.json
results.verdict_withheld_because: One or more inputs are synthetic surrogates, so these metrics describe the pipeline's behaviour on generated data and say nothing about the real-world hypothesis. See data_provenance.json.
